title: Diet, sport and fitness
subtitle: cholesterol, burn calories, sail through
summary: Talk about diet and exercise in precise terms - arteries, fibre, metabolism and BMI - and use the sporting metaphors English borrows for everyday life.

lesson.heading: A healthy heart
lesson.text: Our **arteries** circulate blood around the body. The blood flow can be **impeded** - slowed down or made difficult - by fatty **plaque**, an unwanted substance that forms on the surface of the arteries and can **clog** them, that is, cause them to become blocked. Clogged blood vessels can lead to a **heart attack** or a **stroke**.

examples.text: The most important thing is not to **impede** the flow of blood.
The production of plaque is associated with high levels of **cholesterol**.
examples.note: cholesterol = a fatty substance found in body tissue and blood

lesson.heading: Nutritious but cholesterol-rich
lesson.text: Some foods, such as eggs and shellfish, are **nutritious** - they contain substances your body needs to stay healthy - but they are also **cholesterol-rich**. Eaten **in moderation**, they do not significantly raise cholesterol levels or **pose a danger**.

examples.text: **Cholesterol-rich** foods are fine if eaten **in moderation**.
These foods do not necessarily **pose a danger** to health.

lesson.note: The pattern -rich after a noun and high- before one both mean 'with a lot of': protein-rich, vitamin-rich; high-fibre, high-energy, high-calorie.

lesson.heading: Fibre
lesson.text: 'Bad cholesterol' is **counteracted** by **fibre** in our diet, the substance in foods such as fruit and brown bread which travels through the body as waste. Fibre causes less fat to be absorbed by the blood vessels, so a **high-fibre** diet is often recommended.

examples.text: **Fibre-rich** foods include fruit, vegetables, **lentils**, **oatmeal**, potatoes and wholemeal bread.
examples.note: lentils = very small dried beans; oatmeal = a grain used to make porridge

lesson.heading: Exercise and calories
lesson.text: One of the most efficient forms of **cardiovascular** exercise - exercise relating to the heart and blood - is running or fast walking. It **lowers your blood pressure** and helps **diabetics** too, by helping their **insulin** work more effectively.

examples.text: Running is a good form of **cardiovascular** exercise.
**Brisk** walking is also good for you.
**Diabetics** suffer from diabetes, an illness in which the body cannot cope with glucose because it does not produce enough **insulin**.

lesson.heading: Burning calories
lesson.text: Running is a great way to **burn calories**, and you don't have to be excessively **sporty** - good at or keen on sports - to do it. Exercise can also speed up your **metabolism**, the rate at which your body digests food, and help to lower your **BMI**, or Body Mass Index, the amount of fat in your body as a proportion of your weight.

examples.text: Jogging is a great way to **burn calories**.
A person who weighs 63 kilos can **burn** 148 **calories** by jogging for 20 minutes.
If you're **intent on** losing weight, running and fast cycling are excellent ways of doing so.

lesson.heading: Sport and fitness metaphors
rows: try to gain an advantage but make things worse for yourself
change the rules while things are in progress
level with each other and equally likely to win
pass or complete it very easily

lesson.heading: The metaphors in use
lesson.text: These expressions are common in ordinary conversation and in the press, especially about work and politics.

examples.text: I **scored an own goal** when I told my boss it had only taken me a day to write the report. Now she wants several a week.
My boss always seems to be **moving the goalposts**, which makes it difficult to know what he wants.
The new laws aim to provide **a level playing field** for all member states.
The two main parties are still **neck and neck** in the opinion polls.
The students all **sailed through** their exams.

lesson.text: Impede slows something down; clog blocks it completely.

exercises.explanation: Nutritious food contains substances your body needs to stay healthy.

exercises.explanation: To impede something is to slow it down or make it difficult.

exercises.explanation: To pose a danger is to cause a problem - a standard collocation.

exercises.prompt: Running is a good form of ___ exercise.
exercises.explanation: Cardiovascular exercise works the heart and the circulation.

exercises.prompt: ___ walking is also good for you.
exercises.explanation: Brisk means quick and energetic; we talk about a brisk walk or brisk walking.

To do this kind of exercise you don't have to be excessively ___ .
exercises.explanation: Sporty means good at or keen on sports.

exercises.explanation: Your metabolism is the rate at which your body digests food.
